title: Bremen at Dort: grave falls cost good conscience; lighter daily sins do not
source_text: XVIII. Porro Britannis istis Theologis Reformatos caeteros quoad rem ipsam consentire ostendere non est difficile. Nam in illis ipsis Actis Synodi Dordracenae Theologi Bremenses, in suo circa eundem articulum judicio Thesi undecima docent, Renatos quum in gravia aliqua peccata labuntur, bonam conscientiam, cordis puritatem, & laetitiam spiritus, amittere; quod ipsis non accidit, quum in peccata leviora quotidie incurrunt.
pass_a_gloss: Further it is not hard to show that the rest of the Reformed agree with those British theologians as to the thing itself. For in those very Acts of the Synod of Dort the Bremen theologians, in their judgment on the same article, teach in the eleventh Thesis that when the regenerate fall into some grave sins they lose a good conscience, purity of heart, and gladness of spirit; which does not happen to them when they daily fall into lighter sins.
pass_b_english: Bremen’s Dort eleventh thesis matches Britain: grave falls strip conscience, purity, and joy.
Daily lighter slips do not work that loss.

choices.why: Real loss in grave fall, not mere feeling.
